topics.title: Closing Perspective
topics.summary: Expert C++ engineering is not defined by using the most advanced feature or the fastest processor available. It is defined by making mechanisms explicit enough to reason about them. The CPU, GPU, operating system, compiler, libraries, scheduler, and workload all participate in the observed result. The engineer's task is to preserve correctness across those boundaries while using measurement to decide where complexity is justified.

blocks.text: The progression of this series therefore ends where production work begins: with contracts, evidence, and repeatability. A kernel that is fast but numerically wrong is not an optimization. A pipeline that meets average throughput while growing an unbounded queue is not stable. A real-time claim without a defined deadline and measured distribution is not a timing contract. A build that cannot be reproduced is not a dependable release.
